So I'm going into this game one last time, player base is dead and we're at a 60% discount and free weekend. This has not affected the game's player base at all, and above all, the game is still not fun.

I've never played a game in my life that feels like a chore. There's just a lot of busy work with uninspired levels, playing co-op where there are no one to join your squad. And guess what? If nobody joins and you start anyway there are no bots to help like in L4D2 from 17 years ago - a much better game.

Every "mission" that you do feels uninspired, like a brainstorming session from some indy high school project, or "hackaton" or similar. It doesn't feel like a Remedy product at all, but more like a way for some business major to make a quick buck using ChatGPT to design a game.

FBC Firebreak is just a horde shooter where you hold in tiny sections against the "hiss" from Control completing various chores by hitting the E and Q button. This is where the game really falters, the level design and gameplay is so terribly bad and small that it feels like a demo or an Alpha build. Everybody playing this game asks themselves the same question "where the hell is the rest of the game?"

The weapons feel very underpowered and weak, like shooting peas at the enemies. You don't feel that "meaty" feeling of mowing down enemies like in L4D2, here we just run around and fart at the enemies. It just isn't fun. I can't stress this enough, this is a game devoid of all sense of fun, it is just plane boring, and I get flashbacks to doing menial service jobs in my early 20's.

If you go into this with an unlimited weekend of time you'll have 100% this game on the first day. This game instantly died on release, and various game mods draws a fraction of loyal players back into the game - or just the curious wondering "is it good yet?".

No, no it isn't and it never will be.

Sniper Elite: Resistance feels more like a large expansion for Sniper Elite 5 than a standalone game. 
The campaign puts players in the role of Harry Hawker and, honestly, I hope Rebellion never lets whoever wrote some of his dialogue do it again. Hawker is one of the blandest protagonists in the series, and very little about him makes him memorable. 

Unfortunately, Resistance inherits almost all of the problems that plagued Sniper Elite 5. The AI remains weak, the sniping mechanics are still oversimplified, and many of the design decisions that disappointed fans of earlier entries are still present. 

The one area where I think the developers listened to player feedback is map design. The maps generally offer more opportunities for long-range engagements and provide better sniper positions than many of the locations in Sniper Elite 5. For a game called Sniper Elite, that is a welcome improvement. 
Sadly, that is where most of the positives end. At its core, Resistance is the same game as Sniper Elite 5. It reuses the same mechanics, the same formula, and many of the same flaws while charging a price that is difficult to justify.

If you were disappointed by Sniper Elite 5, Resistance is unlikely to change your mind. If you enjoyed Sniper Elite 5, you may find some value here, but I would still recommend waiting for a significant discount.

In my opinion, Resistance should have been a DLC rather than a standalone release.

I used to love this game.  Played through to the teapot four times!  I loved being an ecosystem engineer with my mobile clinic of plants, animals and insects to rescue degraded islands.  And most of all, loved the AGENCY I had as a player.  Sure, I had to hit up the special unlock islands but other than that I could visit the rest of the game world in any order.

The Bloom & Blight update nerfed a lot of player agency.  The base side of things (building, crafting, farming) is still good when you finally manage to unlock the techs.  But getting those unlocks is quite regimented, and a bit harsh.  Progression may look like a tree, but it acts more like a numbered checklist.  There are step-by-step guides on the workshop to teach the ideal unlock order but even then you'll be forced to choose between two timely and essential unlocks.  For example: combat buffs from cooking -OR- farming sheep.  Make a wrong choice and progression is on hold until you pass the time-consuming 'visit these specific islands in this order before proceeding' chore.  

In my house we've started calling Aloft "Backtrackia."  That's the effect of the restrictive progression system.  A lot of time spent sailing backwards to the islands with stuff we weren't allowed to make use of when we first passed through the area.

If you are tolerant of all the gate keeping it's otherwise a lovely game.  I'm not, so for me that only saving grace is legacy version of the game under Betas.

I'd like to be able to recommend this game, but it's plainly unfinished and suffers from a wide variety of bugs, a lack of endgame content, and a profound lack of QOL features.

Here are some examples:

- Employees frequently idle for extended periods for no obvious reasons.
- Traffic AI is bad enough to cause reliable jams that you are then obliged to fix yourself.
- God help you if you order a bunch of books at once. None of them come boxed up, they can't be boxed, you can't upgrade your ability to manually hold objects, and consequently this is immensely tedious.
- Advertisement is unclear with regard to when your payouts arrive and can be collected, and this also applies to automatically paying employees.
- Price Setting is barely required or worth doing. It is barely affected by your rising rating, and while it does work as intended as far as customer failure-chance, there's absolutely no reason to ever use less than 100% chance, since you can dismiss extra customers for free, juggle them by asking them to wait, or simply accept the popularity cost, since it has no real benefit.
- Cars don't appear to function or have any purpose. I bought all three, have no idea where they went or what they're for, and attempting to leave the motel by the road causes the game to teleport me back to the play area. No idea what the cars are for, or do.
- Warehouse Shelves can be set to specific products, but there's no ability to set warehouse shelves to things like blankets, sheets, or towels. This means that your warehouse will, always and inevitably, become a cluttered nightmare mess of random boxes everywhere, and this is even more true if you have any employees working in the warehouse.
- The Store gameplay is very basic. I don't necessarily have a huge problem with this in isolation, but in the context of the game, it just becomes very clear that this is intended to be executed via employees, the same way as the Gas Station
- Employees do work as intended with regard to the Patience Timers, but what I find really strange is that they have very specific locations where they idle, and do not communicate well as far as tasks or inventory go. I can watch my housekeepers sprint back and forth from the warehouse to the various motel rooms, carrying single objects, and wonder whether they are worth the paychecks at all. Additionally, Employees stop working if their paycheck exceeds $300. This wouldn't be a catastrophic deal, except that the auto-pay system works daily, and occasionally, will not pay employee wages in time to prevent them from going to rest. Once this happens, their assignment clears, and you have to manually reset their entire behavior from your PC. This is inconvenient, annoying, and honestly just adds bloat to an otherwise remarkable framework.
- Finally, decorating is a chore. Most of the decorating in this game is broken up by extremely tedious systems that you need to interact with to accomplish any kind of decoration. As previously mentioned, you have a very limited carrying capacity, and the carts are a chore to use except for items you need to deploy in bulk, like paints, floors, and ceilings. Many items which can become a box within the warehouse,  expand to full size on a cart, resulting in an impossible task of loading too many refridgerators onto a cart that is too small for them, but simultaneously allowing you to carry five of them in your hands. These systems make the highlight of the endgame feel tedious and inconvenient, and not worth participating in, which is a shame, because the mechanics surrounding decorating the rooms (as far as they relate to customer pleasure) is actually kinda cool and interesting. For me, this is the critical failure of Motel Manager Simulator.

Conclusion: This game showed promise, but instead of being a labor of love, it was clearly abandoned a year ago, and has received no attention despite a plethora of bugs, some serious QOL issues, and some balancing problems. I can't recommend it in good conscience unless the developer shows some initiative in getting the game to a more playable state.

With that said, I am still a sucker for games like this, and it'll probably take me some time to fully disentangle myself from this disappointment.

Let's get this straight: this is not Sniper Elite 6, and it barely feels like a proper DLC to Sniper Elite 5.

I have played every Sniper Elite game, and the modern ones in co-op with a friend. Resistance feels like someone took the Sniper Elite 5 engine exactly as it was, kept all its old bugs, and gave it to a much less experienced gameplay and level design team. That is probably why it is not called Sniper Elite 6.

The biggest problem is the AI. It feels like a considerable regression from Sniper Elite 4 and 5, and it makes the game way too easy.

Enemies never use the alarms. There are alarm systems everywhere for you to disable, but what is the point if nobody ever triggers them? There are basically no reinforcements either, apart from maybe one or two scripted events where a truck arrives with four to six soldiers, and even that is not threatening.

You can just start shooting loudly and enemies often come one by one through the same path until they are all dead. Nobody surrounds you, no serious counterattack develops, and there is almost no feeling that the enemy is reacting intelligently to your presence.

In Sniper Elite 3 to 5, I felt under constant threat. I wanted to stay hidden, break lights, avoid alarms, move bodies, set traps and plan for failure.

That planning mattered because resources and inventory space were limited. Choosing one more mine instead of a bandage mattered. Spending a talent point to carry more equipment mattered.

Here it does not.

There are barely any roaming vehicles, no meaningful reinforcements, and almost no reason to mine a road. At the same time, explosives are everywhere. After looting only a few soldiers or rooms, my inventory is already full of ammo, mines, medical supplies and almost everything else, even on the hardest difficulty. I could practically mine every road on the map, but for what?

The same problem applies to traps. I used to enjoy rigging bodies or preparing an ambush in case a patrol found them later. Here, once the nearby soldiers are dead, almost nobody is coming.

Even VIP targets behave stupidly. Instead of fleeing the map or hiding somewhere secure, which gave you a real reason to remain stealthy in previous games, I have seen scientists grab a gun and come outside to hunt me after I already killed dozens of guards.

So the game gives you more tools than ever while removing most of the situations where those tools were useful. Nothing feels scarce, preparation barely matters, and very little feels rewarding.

Talents have the same problem. You can revive yourself, shoot while downed, carry plenty of supplies and replenish almost everything constantly. Most upgrades simply do not feel important.

Weapons also lack personality. I noticed surprisingly little difference between rifles, ammunition types or many weapon modifications. Even the sniping itself somehow feels less rewarding and more arcade-like than before.

Then there is the HUD, which keeps one of my biggest problems with Sniper Elite 5.

The game offers a million difficulty and realism options, yet there is no sensible middle ground for the HUD. Either I get too much arcade information, including indicators showing when enemies are spotting me and text literally explaining what the AI is doing, or I disable so much that I also lose basic information like my health and remaining ammunition.

And no, "just play without the HUD" does not solve this.

In real life I know how many magazines, grenades and other items I have on my belt or in my backpack. Hiding that information is not realism, especially when the game has no proper tactical inventory screen where I can simply check what I am carrying.

I just want to know my health, ammo and equipment without the game also telling me what every enemy around me is thinking.

Sniping has a similar problem. Even with my sniping settings pushed toward maximum realism, the game still gives too much assistance and too much indication of where the shot should go. Combined with the weak AI and lack of danger, it feels more like an arcade mechanic than something I really had to judge and earn.

Then there are the bugs. Many Sniper Elite 5 bugs are still present, with new ones added. Traps attached to electrical panels sometimes simply do not explode, for example.

The world also feels lifeless. There is little interesting dialogue to overhear, little environmental storytelling, and almost nobody except soldiers waiting to be killed.

The two things I still appreciate are that the campaign can be played entirely in co-op with a friend, and that you can save almost anywhere instantly. Unfortunately, when the game provides so little resistance, even the excellent save system becomes much less important.

I am genuinely disappointed because Sniper Elite is a great series and the basic engine is still very good. But Resistance removes much of what made the previous games interesting: tension, stealth, preparation, scarcity, meaningful loadouts, intelligent enemy reactions and rewarding sniping.

I cannot recommend it, even on sale. I would rather wait and hope Rebellion comes back with a proper Sniper Elite 6.
